[b]Ministry of the Interior[/b]

[u]Grand Majlis Passes Islamic Socialism Policy to Replace Previous State-Capitalist System[/u]

After years of negotiations between various political parties, organizations, unions, and vigorous debates in the Grand Majlisi, the implementation of the Islamic Socialist system has passed by a 65% to 35% vote in the Grand Majlisi today. 

Islamic Socialism is economically democratic socialism with some more leeway for small and individual owned enterprises to operate autonomously, as well as personal property ownership being legal. 

However, the Islamic system still in place in all other spheres, the same as under the state-capitalist model. It is not rooted in Marxism and does not legislate anything that is prohibited under the Sharia or in violation of minority religions legal systems. 

This is the natural outcome of the frivolous, rent-seeking, and ultimately selfish and corrupt decisions of the private sector under the previous system. Baladullah couldnt continue to provide a truly fair, just, moral, and ethical socioeconomic system for all people while the capitalist class had so much influence and control in the economy. 

When the top 100 corporations threatened to leave earlier this year unless there were major privatizations and rollbacks on regulations and wage cuts, the Grand Majlisi decided by a single vote to give in to their demands. What we saw was a major increase in income inequality, attacks on unions, a significant increase in class tensions, and a rise in poverty. This time, when Daguo corporations and nativist corporations were about to get into a legal war over ownership and investment, the Grand Majlisi said enough. 

In shaa Allah, this will be better for our people and bring back more economic and social justice that we lost when we carried out the capitalist reforms of the state-capitalist system. - Abdullah ibn Ibrahim al-Ikhwani, Wazir of the Council of Emirs
God Bless the King
